description: Structured eval definitions for the EKS Add-On Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across EKS add-on scenarios (core add-ons on new cluster, EBS CSI with IRSA, Pod Identity for ADOT, Auto Mode manual override blocked, version conflict migration). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: Core EKS add-ons (vpc-cni, coredns, kube-proxy) on new EKS 1.30 cluster with IRSA
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — core networking add-ons, K8s 1.30 version compatibility, IRSA for vpc-cni, ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION config, conflict resolution OVERWRITE
eval_cases.prompt: I have a new EKS cluster named production-cluster running Kubernetes 1.30. I need to set up the core add-ons: vpc-cni, coredns, and kube-proxy. The cluster has an OIDC provider. For vpc-cni I want to use IRSA with the AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy. I want ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION set to true. Account ID: 123456789012. Tags: Environment=production.
eval_cases.expected_output:
EKS_ADDON: vpc-cni (version v1.18.1-eksbuild.3) on cluster production-cluster
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Cluster: production-cluster — ACTIVE, Kubernetes 1.30
  [✓] Add-on type: vpc-cni
  [✓] Add-on version: v1.18.1-eksbuild.3 (compatible with K8s 1.30)
  [✓] Management mode: EKS-managed
  [✓] Conflict resolution: OVERWRITE
  [✓] Configuration values: {"env":{"ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION":"true"}}
  [✓] IAM credential method: IRSA (role AmazonEKSVPCCNIRole)
  [✓] OIDC provider: present
  [✓] Auto Mode cluster: no
  [✓] Health: ACTIVE
  [✓] Tags: Environment=production
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws eks describe-addon --cluster-name production-cluster --addon-name vpc-cni
  aws eks list-addons --name production-cluster
  kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=aws-node

eval_cases.name: EBS CSI driver add-on with IRSA for PersistentVolume provisioning

eval_cases.expected_output:
EKS_ADDON: aws-ebs-csi-driver (version v1.26.0-eksbuild.1) on cluster app-cluster
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Cluster: app-cluster — ACTIVE, Kubernetes 1.29
  [✓] Add-on type: aws-ebs-csi-driver
  [✓] Add-on version: v1.26.0-eksbuild.1 (compatible with K8s 1.29)
  [✓] Management mode: EKS-managed
  [✓] Conflict resolution: OVERWRITE
  [✓] IAM credential method: IRSA (role AmazonEBSCSIDriverRole)
  [✓] Service account: ebs-csi-controller-sa (kube-system)

eval_cases.name: EKS Pod Identity for ADOT collector add-on
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — Pod Identity Agent installed, Pod Identity association for ADOT in observability namespace, pods.eks.amazonaws.com trust principal
eval_cases.prompt: I want to use EKS Pod Identity (not IRSA) for my ADOT collector add-on on cluster observability-cluster (K8s 1.30). Install the Pod Identity Agent, create a Pod Identity role, and associate it with the ADOT service account in the observability namespace. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
EKS_ADDON: adot (version v0.92.1-eksbuild.1) on cluster observability-cluster
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Cluster: observability-cluster — ACTIVE, Kubernetes 1.30
  [✓] Add-on type: adot
  [✓] Management mode: EKS-managed
  [✓] IAM credential method: Pod Identity (association in observability namespace)
  [✓] Pod Identity Agent: eks-pod-identity-agent installed
  [✓] Trust principal: pods.eks.amazonaws.com
  [✓] Health: ACTIVE
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws eks describe-addon --cluster-name observability-cluster --addon-name adot
  aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name observability-cluster
  aws eks describe-addon --cluster-name observability-cluster --addon-name eks-pod-identity-agent

eval_cases.name: Operator manually updates vpc-cni on EKS Auto Mode cluster (blocked)
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — Auto Mode manages vpc-cni automatically; manual changes are silently reverted by reconciliation
eval_cases.prompt: My EKS cluster auto-mode-cluster uses EKS Auto Mode. I want to manually update the vpc-cni add-on to version v1.19.0-eksbuild.1 and set ENABLE_IPv6 to true. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
EKS_ADDON: vpc-cni on cluster auto-mode-cluster
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Auto Mode cluster: yes — vpc-cni is managed by EKS Auto Mode. Manual add-on creation/updates are silently reverted by Auto Mode reconciliation. Use cluster-level networking settings instead of add-on configuration values.
  [✗] Configuration values: ENABLE_IPv6 must be set via cluster-level settings, not via --configuration-values on a managed add-on.
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws eks describe-cluster --name auto-mode-cluster --query 'cluster.computeConfig'
  aws eks describe-addon --cluster-name auto-mode-cluster --addon-name vpc-cni --query 'addon.status'

eval_cases.name: Migrate self-managed vpc-cni to EKS-managed with config preservation
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — self-managed to EKS-managed migration, OVERWRITE conflict resolution, configuration-values migration pattern, customizations preserved
eval_cases.prompt: My cluster migration-cluster (K8s 1.30) has a self-managed vpc-cni installed via Helm (the aws-node DaemonSet). I have custom env vars: AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_LOGLEVEL=DEBUG and ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION=true. I want to migrate to the EKS-managed vpc-cni add-on without losing my customizations. OIDC provider exists. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
EKS_ADDON: vpc-cni (version v1.18.1-eksbuild.3) on cluster migration-cluster
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Cluster: migration-cluster — ACTIVE, Kubernetes 1.30
  [✓] Add-on type: vpc-cni
  [✓] Management mode: EKS-managed (migrated from self-managed)
  [✓] Conflict resolution: OVERWRITE (migration)
  [✓] Configuration values: {"env":{"AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_LOGLEVEL":"DEBUG","ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION":"true"}}
  [✓] IAM credential method: IRSA (role AmazonEKSVPCCNIRole)
  [✓] Self-managed add-on: present (resolving with OVERWRITE, re-applying config via configuration-values)
  [✓] Health: ACTIVE
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws eks describe-addon --cluster-name migration-cluster --addon-name vpc-cni
  kubectl get ds -n kube-system aws-node
  kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=aws-node
